summary: LMAT is a fundamentally non-distressed mid-cap medical-device serial acquirer with zero going-concern signals, a 10-year clean Grant Thornton tenure, unqualified ICFR, no critical audit matters, no customer concentration (max 2%), and a 25% dividend hike (Feb 2025). However, multiple Mode-B disclosure gaps merit attention: (1) $172.5M convertible note raise Dec 2024 layered on $300M of existing cash with no specified use of proceeds and no capped call; (2) ~$37M of discretionary insider open-market selling across CEO/CFO/directors 2024-01 to 2025-05-14 with zero corresponding buyback execution despite $50M (2024) and $75M (2025) board authorizations; (3) long-tenured CFO Pellegrino retiring March 2025 coinciding with new D365 ERP rollout and post-issuance of converts, after he sold $2.6M in March 2024; (4) Q1 2025 operating income growth decelerated to +6.3% from +42% FY24 — not reset in MD&A narrative. Tariff exposure to ex-US distribution is acknowledged but unquantified. Read: non-distressed business but adverse insider/capital-raise signals offset bullish dividend hike; net neutral.
